title: Provenance-enhanced metric fanout for inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: unify and extend the metrics collection pipeline so that custom inference KPIs (per-request latency, model_variant error-rate, token-cost attribution) carry provenance metadata through OTLP -> ingestion -> Prometheus-exposed rollups and downstream SLO calculators. We want deterministic routing for tenant-aware rollups, stable exemplar linking to traces, and a fanout that supports both aggregate global KPIs and per-tenant, per-route derivatives with bounded cardinality.

Motivation: current pipeline drops or anonymizes fields early (route/model tags) when converting OTLP to Prometheus, forcing joins later and creating imprecise SLOs and billing attributions. This ticket adds a provenance layer: a compact, schema-versioned envelope attached to KPI events that survives aggregation, supports sketching/rollup policies, and enables reconstructing the request lineage for root-cause analysis.

Scope:
- Define a small provenance schema (schema v1) containing request_id, model_variant, route, deployment_tier, tenant_id_hash, sampling_reason. This lives as attribute tags on OTLP metrics and as Prometheus labels where feasible.
- Implement provenance enrichment in the front-line metric producer (inference sidecar) so every KPI includes the envelope.
- Extend the ingestion fanout (metric-gateway) to: (1) route enriched metrics to tenant-specific rollup pipelines, (2) attach exemplars for high-latency/error events to traces, (3) apply deterministic reservoir sharding for histograms to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Add a transformation layer that collapses low-cardinality provenance (e.g., deployment_tier) into Prometheus labels and sketches high-cardinality fields (tenant_id_hash) into separate lookup tables to keep prometheus label cardinality bounded.
- Update downstream SLO calculators to consume the enriched rollups and add a migration path for existing SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test: a synthetic request produces an OTLP metric with provenance, we can see a Prometheus-exposed timeseries for the aggregated KPI and click through an exemplar to a trace.
- No more than 5% increase in ingestion CPU for steady-state workloads for the default sampling config.
- Prometheus label cardinality growth constrained to <10% for typical tenants (validated with tenant-sim harness).
- Backwards compatible: unlabeled legacy metrics still processed and mapped to safest default provenance fields.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable provenance envelope and exemplar attachment for 5% of traffic in a non-prod cluster; collect ingest load and cardinality metrics.
- Phase 2 (region rollout): expand to edge regions with tenant simulation, enable deterministic reservoir sharding.
- Phase 3 (full): enable tenant-aware rollups and switch SLO calculators to consume enriched rollups, deprecate legacy path after 8 weeks.

Observability & validation:
- Add dashboards: Provenance Fanout Health (ingest throughput, CPU, queue latency), Provenance Cardinality (label counts per region), Exemplar Linkage Success Rate.
- Synthetic test harness: replay recorded request traces with mapped model variants and routes to validate aggregation fidelity.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Provenance+Metric+Fanout+Design (internal)
- Simulation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-sim/tree/eng-204983
- Proposed Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/provenance-fanout
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metric-gateway/pull/1294

Notes on trade-offs and open questions:
- We intentionally avoid placing tenant_id as a raw label in Prometheus to prevent cardinality blowup; using tenant_id_hash + lookup allows precise attribution without unbounded labels but requires consistent hashing across producers.
- Exemplar storage and lookup may increase storage; proposal uses a TTLd exemplar store keyed by request_id. Long-term we may integrate with trace storage to avoid duplication.
- Deterministic reservoir sharding reduces noisy histogram merging but requires coordination algorithm; initial plan uses consistent hashing with a small shard count per ingestion node.
- Security: provenance data contains tenant_id_hash but not raw PII. We flagged a potential need for security review if we want to include user-identifying fields later.

Next steps: finalize schema v1, land inference sidecar enrichment PR, add exemplar plumbing in metric-gateway, set up canary and dashboards.
